title: Posting at fair minus cushion minus fee sits ~4.6c under the mid behind ~77x its own size; fills need a level pull or a sweep, not flow
claim: sharp_direct orders average 4.56c below the venue mid with 8,524 contracts resting ahead against a 110-contract order; constrained 5.4c and 5,353; sharp_two_sided 0.8c and 15,336 (the two-sided column's side conversion for NO orders is unverified). The tape carries ~20 trades/min across 500 subscribed tickers overnight (max 75), so an average ticker prints tens of trades a day; consuming 8,500 contracts at one level takes longer than the order's life. min_volume_24h=50 rejected 25 of 34,100 signal rows in the LAR-SF window and does not discriminate fillability; queue_ahead/volume_24h does and is unfiltered. The 2c edge floor plus 1c AS seed plus ~0.44c fee puts every target >=3.4c under fair, which on a calibrated venue is under the best bid on NFL books (spread <= 8c).
question: viability
evidence: evidence G per variant: 5632da729fa7 mid_minus_price 0.0081 queue_ahead 15,336 contracts 110.4; f259ca109084 0.0456 / 8,524 / 109.6; ff363c8ac08d 0.0543 / 5,353 / 137.3
evidence J: ws.trades_per_min avg 19.6 max 75 over 500 tickers (6 h, night); venue_trades 494,386 rows/24 h
evidence H: volume rejected 25 of 34,100 rows; source_allowed 19,203; has_fair 12,983; candidates 930 (2.7%)
harness/strategy/run.py:308-312 p0 = fair - edge_min - as; price_target = snap_to_grid(p0 - fee); edge label requires price_target < best_ask
harness/variants/sharp_direct.yaml edge_floor 0.02, as_seed 0.01, min_volume_24h 50, max_spread_c nfl 8 / ncaaf 20
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-06-sportsbook-harness-design.md §3 rows 2-4: Kalshi inside 48 h close to calibrated; maker fee up to 44% of a 1-point edge so the floor is 2 points
evidence G order 157: queue_ahead_at_place 6,401 at 0.45 with venue bid/ask 0.48/0.49; filled only after the level was pulled
recommendation: Add queue_ahead/volume_24h and time-to-kickoff to table 6 as the fillability panel and, as an executor-policy amendment (plan.py:602-604 ordering), rank intents for the capacity cap by expected fillability (small queue_ahead relative to volume, near kickoff) rather than descending edge. A join-the-bid or near-kickoff variant is only possible as a new id by dated pre-registration amendment (invariant 1); do not touch the seven registered files.
corrections: sharp_direct orders average 4.56c below the venue mid (YES space, YES-only variant) with 8,524 contracts resting at their own price level ahead of a 110-contract order (~78x); constrained 5.4c and 5,353 (137-contract orders); sharp_two_sided 15,336 ahead, but its 0.8c mid-distance column is invalid, not merely unverified, because venue_mid_at_place is stored in YES space (loop.py:1025-1027) while prob is in side space (plan.py:139-141), so NO rows are miscomputed. The WS tape carried 19.6 trades/min (max 75) across 500 subscribed tickers over 6 overnight hours (evidence J), ~56 prints/ticker/day at that rate; venue_trades records 494,386 rows/24 h exchange-wide (REST plus WS), so the daytime per-ticker rate is unverified. Consuming 8,500 contracts at one level is not plausible within the median 12.2 min / mean 33.7 min order life on the one measured market (order 157: 63.92 contracts printed at the level in 30 min, 88.92 over ~2 days), and its only queue_model fill came after >= ~6,300 contracts were cancelled from the 6,401-deep level (fills.py:290-320), not from flow. rejection_reason='volume' was the first failing label on 25 of 34,100 signal rows in the LAR-SF window (first-False attribution, run.py:28-38/372-376), so min_volume_24h=50 almost never binds; queue_ahead/volume_24h is not a filter (run.py LABEL_ORDER has no queue term). The 2c edge floor plus 1c AS seed plus 0.28-0.44c maker fee, floored to the cent grid, puts every target >= ~3.3-3.4c under fair with no best_bid test (run.py:312 tests only price_target < best_ask); on a calibrated venue that is below the best bid whenever the spread is under ~6.8c, and on average (4.56c) it is below the bid on any NFL book within the 8c spread cap; 73% of orders are NCAAF (5,811/7,997) where the cap is 20c.

sharp_direct (YES-only) orders average 4.56c below the venue mid with an order-weighted mean of 8,524 contracts resting at their exact price level against a 110-contract order (constrained 5.4c / 5,353; the sharp_two_sided 0.8c figure is invalid because venue_mid_at_place is YES-space while prob is side-space, loop.py:1027; medians unverified until the table 6 report). The realized cushion is larger than the 3.4c floor: edge_at_place averages 4.22c because edge_min = 2c + 1.5 x disagreement (up to 6c when only one book group), so targets sit ~4.66c under fair and fair ~= venue mid + 0.1c on average; the posted edge is entirely cushion. By construction (book.resting_at = depth at our price; fills.py _apply_print/_apply_queue_delta) a queue_model fill needs the best bid to fall to our level and the level to trade out or be pulled, or a sweep through it, which is the spec's intended slow-maker/adverse-selection design (spec §3 rows 3-4, §6.3, R12) and a measurement the weekly report already makes. Under the current cancel policy (fair_stale p50 12.2 min in book, 220 s allowance vs 1-3.5 min fair refreshes) fills are near-impossible; the no_watcher counterfactual (646 fill rows / 18,512 contracts vs 38.92 real, 27 of 445 market-sides so far) shows longer order life would produce fills, but they would be level reaches (adverse selection), not flow fills. Tape rate: the 19.6 trades/min figure is the overnight window; venue_trades runs 494k rows/24 h (~343/min), concentrated on the ~500 subscribed tickers, and contracts per trade are unverified. The volume filter rejected 25 of the ~1,900 rows that reached it (rejection_reason is the first false label), not 25 of 34,100; the claim that queue_ahead/volume_24h discriminates fillability is unverified at n = 1 fill. Order 157's fill came after its 6,401-contract queue went to zero without prints at its price (cancels or the dirty-book resync; book_dirty was true on every watch sample), consistent with a level pull.

Severity: important (the single most material viability finding; not critical only because the week-3 success criterion at spec line 258 is a snapshot-CLV mispricing map that needs no fills). The target-price rule at harness/strategy/run.py:308-310 posts sharp_direct ~4.6c under the venue mid behind ~78x its own size (evidence G: 0.0456 / 8,524 vs 109.6 contracts), the tape runs ~20 trades/min over 500 tickers (evidence J), and only 27 of 445 distinct posts would have filled even if never cancelled (controller note 10), so the 1-fill-in-3-days book is structural and the go-live gate's 150 print-confirmed fills (spec line 254) is unreachable under the current posting policy; the owner should treat fillability, not fair_stale churn, as the strategy question for the Monday 2026-09-14 report and decide any pre-registered join-the-bid / near-kickoff variant before the week-2 freeze on 2026-09-21 (roadmap line 55).
